messages:
Alex Chen: Ran scheduled bench after kernel swap (attn opt). p50 unchanged, p95 +10ms, p99 +36ms, p999 +120ms. attaching harness output. bench-id 20260320-42
Maria Gomez: ugh. did you run the same workload shard? config same as before?
Alex Chen: same harness, same seed. Command: `./bench --suite=tail-latency --model=redwood-3b-quant --seed=42 --concurrency=8 --dur=600`
Samir Patel: logs? any CPU thrashing / memcpy spikes
Alex Chen: pasted snippet:
```
latency p99: 82ms -> 118ms
kv-cache hit rate: 92%
gpu util: 88% -> 90% (nominal)
kernel: fused_attn_v2 -> fused_attn_v3
```
Maria Gomez: kernel swap candidate then. Did platform rollout the kernel to only some nodes? could be hetero mix causing head-of-line.
Jordan (runtime-bot): alert: kernel-version mismatch detected on 3/12 nodes in pool-xy. Deploy id: dpl-20260319-9
Sasha Ilyin: that's consistent. Mixed kernel builds can cause path divergence when batching shapes vary. Repro idea: pin kernel v2 on all nodes and rerun.
Samir Patel: also add deterministic sampling to harness (disable tail sampling). sampling noise can blow p99.
Alex Chen: rerun queued with `--pin-kernel=v2 --no-sampling`. starting now.
QA Bot: smoke finished in 60s. p99 back to baseline (85ms). Looks promising.
Maria Gomez: good. can we diff a single-request trace between v2 and v3? need to see micro-op timing.
Sasha Ilyin: grabbed traces: attaching short trace blocks.
Alex Chen: trace shows an extra memcpy in v3 for attn stride normalization. that's our extra 30-40ms at p99 for some seq shapes.
Samir Patel: ok hypothesis: v3 added stride-correctness memcpy which regresses rare long-shape paths. fix options: 1) conditional memcpy only when needed; 2) precompute layout; 3) fallback to v2 for those shapes.
Maria Gomez: my vote: short-term fallback by kernel selector for shapes > 2048 tokens; long-term: add layout-aware kernel with fast-path.
Jordan (runtime-bot): created ticket INF-847: fallbacks + perf test for stride memcpy. assignee: Sasha.
Sasha Ilyin: taking INF-847. will prototype conditional memcpy+unit tests. planning a canary tomorrow.
Alex Chen: thanks team. leaving thread open for any extra logs. :thumbsup:
